reason: The hypothesis relies on a mechanistic chain (entropy → single-phase → suppressed phase separation → durability) that is directly supported by E2 for OER, but the cited evidence for catalytic activity and durability in automotive exhaust conditions is largely from different reactions (CO oxidation, NH3 decomposition, CO2 hydrogenation) and materials (oxides, supported NPs), with no cited evidence demonstrating reduced PGM consumption in an exhaust catalyst.
premises: High configurational entropy stabilizes a homogeneous single-phase solid solution in HEAs
This single-phase structure suppresses phase separation and secondary phase formation
Suppressed phase separation enhances structural integrity and resistance to corrosion/dissolution
Enhanced structural integrity improves catalytic durability
HEA catalysts can reduce platinum-group-metal consumption while maintaining or improving activity
